column3: The Hebrew does not explicitly name the Jordan in the crossing and uses singular collective “man of Ephraim”; BSB supplies “the Jordan” and has plural “men.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Jephthah called “you” and has singular “their hand”; BSB says “when I called” without the object and uses plural “their hands.”
The Hebrew says Jephthah put his soul in his palm and calls the enemy “sons of Ammon”; BSB has “risked my life” and “the Ammonites.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Ephraim as the defeated group and calls the Gileadites “fugitives of Ephraim”; BSB uses “them” and “fugitives in Ephraim.”
The Hebrew names “Gilead” collectively and uses plural “fugitives of Ephraim”; BSB has “the Gileadites” and singular “a fugitive.”
The Hebrew says forty-two thousand “fell” from Ephraim; BSB uses the passive “were killed.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Jephthah’s name and calls him “the Gileadite”; BSB uses “he” and omits that designation in the death clause.
The Hebrew says “after him”; BSB explicitly names Jephthah.
The Hebrew calls the women brought in “daughters” and says he sent his own daughters “outside”; BSB has “wives” and makes marriage outside the clan explicit.
The Hebrew says “after him” and separately repeats that Elon judged Israel; BSB names Ibzan and combines the judging statements.
The Hebrew says “after him”; BSB explicitly names Elon.
The Hebrew calls the thirty descendants “sons of sons”; BSB says “grandsons.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amalekite”; BSB has plural “the Amalekites.”
